title: Brother Lawrence's conversations
hookLine: he trained himself to return to God's presence whenever he forgot
tomorrow: how little can a prayer be and still count?

cards: You meant to check one thing on your phone. Forty minutes later you surface, not sure where the time went. Or you start the day promising to be patient, and by lunch you've forgotten you promised.
Forgetting isn't a rare failure. It's the default setting. So what do you do about it?
A cook in a French monastery kept forgetting God all day long, and a visitor wrote down what he did.

teach.h: A LAY BROTHER IN A KITCHEN.
teach.b: He's known as Brother Lawrence, a lay brother of the Carmelites, the same order as Teresa and John. He wasn't a priest or a scholar.

In the conversations a visitor named Joseph de Beaufort wrote down, Lawrence calls himself, in effect, a clumsy fellow who broke things. They put him to work in the kitchen, a job he says he naturally disliked.
And there he set himself one practice: to keep turning to God, in the middle of the work, as to a friend in the room. Here's the part people skip.
So what did he do when he noticed he'd drifted? According to the conversations, he didn't punish himself or start a stricter program.
He simply admitted it to God, in effect: this is what I do when I'm left to myself; you'll have to keep me from falling.
Then he gave it no more worry, and turned back. And again.
And again. Over time, he said, the hours of work and the hours of prayer stopped feeling different.
One to tell a friend tonight: he said that in the clatter of the kitchen, with several people calling for different things at once, he could be as calm with God as on his knees in chapel.

how: Brother Lawrence's conversations and letters, gathered as The Practice of the Presence of God, are read by Christians of many churches; readers try to turn to God briefly in the middle of ordinary work.

s: practicing God's presence means you stop getting distracted
Lawrence drifted constantly. the practice was coming back, again and again.
Lawrence worked in the monastery kitchen, a job he says he disliked
and it's where he learned to turn to God in the middle of the work.
when he forgot God, he made up for it with long penances
the conversations say he admitted it plainly, gave it no more worry, and turned back.

games.q: you promised yourself to keep God in mind through a long shift at work. at lunch you realize you forgot all morning. what would Lawrence do?
o: admit it plainly, without fuss, and turn back right then.
write the day off and start over tomorrow with a stricter plan.
make up for the lost morning with an hour of prayer tonight.
games.why: no penalty, no new program. he owned the drift in a sentence and came back, as many times as it took.

practice: Close your eyes and choose one anchor: the word here, or a name of God if you pray. When your mind wanders, and it will, notice it without scolding and come back to the anchor. The returns are the practice, not the stillness.
